transcript.content:
**Trailer Washout Reimbursement Policy**

A washout may be passed through only when the delivered load leaves the trailer needing cleaning for the next pickup. If the trailer did not need a wash for the next load, there is no reimbursement.

How we determine the payable level:
- Use the stronger of:
  - the commodity’s contamination class, and
  - the wash required by operations for the next load.
- Food-grade trailers always require at least a **sanitize** wash.
- Non-contaminating dry freight is not reimbursed unless operations specifically required a wash.

Contract limits:
- Wash levels reimburse up to these maximums:
  - rinse: **$35**
  - standard: **$85**
  - sanitize: **$140**
  - hazmat: **$225**
- A contract may:
  - disallow washout pass-through completely, or
  - allow only the standard maximum when a hazmat wash was required.
- A customer cap, if present, applies before deductible is taken.

Settlement math:
- Reimbursable amount is the lesser of the carrier receipt and the allowed maximum, then reduced by the carrier deductible.
- If the eligible amount is at or below the deductible, reimbursement is **$0.00**.
- Round the final amount to the nearest cent.
- Negative receipts or invalid wash levels are not payable.

Examples:
- **Dry freight, no wash needed:** receipt is $22, but operations did not require a wash. Reimbursement is **$0.00**.
- **Chemical load, standard wash required:** receipt is $100. Standard max is $85, less $15 deductible = **$70.00** reimbursable.

transcript.content:
### Hazmat handling and charges

Hazmat is treated in two separate ways:

- **Placards required on the truck**: this is a dispatch and safety requirement.
- **Hazmat surcharge to the customer**: this is a flat accessorial charge on the load.

#### When placards are required
A load must be placarded if:

- It contains **any Table 1 hazmat material**, even at a small quantity; or
- The **total hazmat weight on the load is 1,001 lb or more**.

Table 1 materials include these hazard classes in our billing rules:
- 1.1, 1.2, 1.3
- 2.3
- 4.3
- 6.1-PIH
- 7

#### When the hazmat surcharge applies
- If a load has **any hazmat at all**, the customer is charged **$150.00 per load**.
- This charge applies **whether or not the load needs placards**.
- The surcharge is **flat**: multiple hazmat items on the same load still generate only one $150.00 charge.

### Examples

- **Example 1:** A load includes a 340 lb aerosol cleaner (UN1950, class 2.1) along with regular freight.  
  - No placards required, because the hazmat is under 1,001 lb and not Table 1.
  - Hazmat surcharge still applies: **$150.00**.

- **Example 2:** A load includes 90 lb of chlorine cylinders (UN1017, class 2.3).  
  - Placards are required immediately, because class 2.3 is a Table 1 material.
  - Hazmat surcharge also applies: **$150.00**.

transcript.name: read_contract_page
transcript.content:
**Trailer periodic inspection due rules**

Tidewater trailers are due for their next shop inspection based on **whichever comes first: calendar days or mileage**. The clock starts from the **last completed inspection**.

### Standard due intervals
- **Standard trailer:** 90 days or 12,000 miles
- **Refrigerated trailer:** 60 days or 10,000 miles
- **Hazmat-spec trailer:** 45 days or 8,000 miles

### California rule
- Trailers based in **California** use a tighter **75-day** calendar limit **only if that is sooner** than the normal calendar limit for the trailer type.
- California does **not** change the mileage limit.

### Failed inspection follow-up
- If the last inspection was **failed**, the trailer must be reinspected in **7 days or 500 miles**, whichever comes first.
- This rule can only **tighten** the normal schedule; it never extends it.

### Holds and overdue status
- If a trailer has an **active roadside defect hold**, it is **immediately overdue**, even if the normal due date or mileage has not arrived.
- A trailer is considered due **on the exact due date or exact due odometer**.
- Odometer readings must never go backward.

### Examples
- **Standard trailer:** Last inspected on Jan 1 at 100,000 miles. On Jan 31 at 104,000 miles, it is **not yet due**. Due point remains **Mar 31 / 112,000 miles**.
- **Failed inspection:** Last inspection failed. If the trailer was last inspected on Jan 1 at 70,000 miles, it becomes due on **Jan 8 or 70,500 miles**, whichever comes first.

When both thresholds are crossed, report how far overdue the trailer is in **days and miles**.

transcript.content:
### Federal axle weight rules for loaded tractor-trailers

Before a truck is dispatched on the Interstate, we verify the scale ticket or planned axle loads against federal limits. A load is legal only if it stays within **all** of these rules:

- **Single axle:** no axle may carry more than **20,000 lbs** unless it is part of a tandem.
- **Tandem axle:** two axles more than 40 inches and no more than 96 inches apart may carry up to **34,000 lbs total**.
- **Gross vehicle weight:** the whole tractor-trailer may not exceed **80,000 lbs**.
- **Bridge/span limits:** every group of two or more consecutive axles must stay within the federal bridge weight formula based on the span between the outer axles and the number of axles in the group.
- **Special double-tandem allowance:** two consecutive tandems may carry **34,000 lbs each** if the outer axles are **36 feet or more apart**, even if the bridge formula is lower.

We treat axle positions front to back, measured from the steer axle. If the positions are not increasing, or there are fewer than two axles, the load plan is not usable.

### What we look for
If a load fails, we flag each problem separately:
- single-axle overload
- tandem overload
- gross overload
- bridge/span overload

### Examples

- **Legal load:** 12,000 / 17,000 / 17,000 / 17,000 / 17,000 lbs at typical five-axle positions can be legal if all tandem, bridge, and gross limits are met.
- **Overweight tandem:** 21,000 on the steer axle and 17,500 + 17,500 on a tandem would be flagged for both the steer axle and the tandem.

transcript.content:
## Random Drug-Testing Pool Requirements

For each testing period, we size the random drug-testing pool based on the number of **eligible CDL drivers** and the **annual random testing rate** in effect for that year.

### Who counts in the pool
Include:
- Active CDL drivers
- Leased owner-operators operating under our authority

Exclude:
- Noncovered drivers
- Drivers on long-term leave of 31 days or more

If the eligible count would go below zero, we treat it as zero.

### How the requirement is set
- If the annual testing rate is **0%**, no selections are required.
- We calculate the annual target by multiplying the eligible driver count by the annual rate.
- The annual target is rounded to a whole driver using standard half-up rounding.
- We subtract any random selections already completed earlier in the year.
- The remaining obligation is spread across the remaining monthly or quarterly periods in the calendar year.
- The current period’s requirement is rounded **up** so we do not defer fractional drivers.
- The final requirement can never be negative and can never exceed the eligible driver count.

### Examples
- **Monthly program:** 100 eligible drivers at a 50% annual rate gives an annual target of 50. In January, with 12 months remaining, the requirement is **5** for the month.
- **Quarterly program:** 40 eligible drivers at a 25% annual rate gives an annual target of 10. If 4 selections were already completed by Q3, 6 remain over 2 quarters, so the current quarter requirement is **3**.

### Important checks
- Negative driver counts or prior selections are not accepted.
- Quarterly periods must be numbered 1 through 4.
- Monthly periods must be numbered 1 through 12.

## Monthly Carrier On-Time Scorecard

This scorecard is sent to each contracted carrier at month end. It is used to track service performance and helps drive tender priority on the Hartline lanes.

### What counts as on time
A delivery is **on time** if it arrives:

- **before the end of the appointment window**, or
- **within 15 minutes after the window ends**

Anything delivered at or before that 15-minute grace mark is still on time.

### What is not measured
Do **not** include these in the on-time percentage:

- **Cancelled loads**
- Loads still **in transit**
- **Late deliveries with an excused delay code**, when the delay was not the carrier’s fault:
  - **CUST** = shipper loaded late
  - **CONS** = consignee refused the appointment
  - **WX** = weather closure

These are shown separately and left out of the percentage entirely.

### How the percentage is calculated
The on-time percentage is based only on:

- on-time deliveries
- unexcused late deliveries

Formula conceptually:

- **On-time % = on-time deliveries ÷ measured deliveries**

If there are **no measured deliveries** in the period, show **n/a** instead of 0%.

### Examples
- A load delivered **10 minutes after** the window ends is **on time**.
- A load delivered **16 minutes after** the window ends is **late**.
- If a load is delivered **45 minutes late** with code **WX**, it is **excused** and **not counted** in the percentage.
- If a month has 7 on-time loads, 2 excused late loads, and 1 unexcused late load, the scorecard is **87.5%** because only the 8 measured loads are included.

CT-206: Bridge axle span violation missing on tandem group
Ops flagged TW-58213 because the axle-weight check is missing a bridge-law violation on one of the recent tandems. The truck is being released as compliant even though the axle group looks too heavy for the span between the steer axle and the rear tandem set, so this could let an overweight unit leave the yard without a warning. Please take a look at the axle-weight review for this load before it is used in dispatch.

Comments:

The special double-tandem allowance (34,000 each) applies only when the outer axles are >= 36 ft apart. Evaluate the bridge weight formula using the span and axle count for the steer-plus-rear-tandem group on TW-58213; a group over the formula must be flagged as a separate bridge/span violation. Add a regression test with a tandem group that exceeds the bridge limit. P1, safety/compliance. Also first in the Hartline go-live chain.

The billing/ops view for trailer inspection follow-up looks wrong on a failed inspection. For trailer TW-58213, the reinspection should be tightened after a fail, but the system is leaving the due date far later than expected even though the mileage limit is already nearly reached. This affects our maintenance tracking because the trailer can appear safely in compliance when it actually needs attention much sooner.

CT-216: Monthly drug testing requirement crashes in final period
One of the monthly drug testing pool calculations is blowing up for a small carrier near the end of the year. For driver pool DRP-4412, the January compliance run for period 12 fails outright instead of returning a capped requirement, so the safety report cannot be completed for that month. This blocks the ops team from finalizing the required random testing count for the carrier.

Comments:
- triage: Triage: confirmed defect. Monthly periods are valid 1-12, so period 12 must compute a capped requirement rather than crash. Annual target = eligible drivers x annual rate, rounded whole half-up; subtract prior selections; spread over remaining periods; round the current period requirement up; final requirement must be >= 0 and <= eligible count. Fix the final-period path for DRP-4412 and add regression tests for period 12 and the eligible-count cap. P1: blocks the carrier's compliance/safety report.

CT-220: Postal codes with ZIP+4 are failing on spreadsheet values
An ops analyst spotted that several customer addresses coming out of the spreadsheet import are not normalizing as valid ZIP+4 codes. Records with a numeric postal code that should be preserved as a plus-four format are getting rejected instead, which breaks address cleanup for mail and delivery paperwork. This is affecting shipment and customer records that rely on those postal codes being standardized correctly.

Comments:
- triage: Triage: confirmed defect. Postal normalization must accept numeric spreadsheet values: strip a trailing .0, restore leading zeros, and treat 9 digits with no hyphen as ZIP+4 (last 4 = extension). Examples: 2134.0 -> 02134; 8601234.0 -> 00860-1234; 972091234 -> 97209-1234. Only reject blank, non-postal garbage, too many digits, or bad ZIP+4 shapes. Fix and add regression tests for numeric plus-four values including the .0 form. P2.

transcript.name: read_ticket
transcript.content:
CT-222: Reefer excursion minutes come up short on gap-ended runs
Ops flagged a reefer excursion on load TW-58213 that is being reported a hair under the expected duration, which is causing the temperature event to fall short in the customer summary. The same thing is showing up on another temperature breach for the same carrier: the event looks right in the timeline, but the billed excursion length is slightly off. This matters because their monitoring and exception workflow keys off the reported minutes, and anything under the threshold can be missed during review.

Comments:
- triage: Triage: confirmed defect to verify. An excursion ends at the first in-range reading; if the logger goes quiet for more than 15 minutes while still out of range, or the data ends while out of range, it ends at the last reading received. Reported minutes should be last-reading time minus first out-of-range time (only excursions >= 30 minutes are reported). A gap-ended run reporting short suggests the final reading or the gap boundary is being dropped. Fix and add a regression test for a gap-ended (not closed) excursion. P2: customer exception workflow keys off these minutes.

drug_testing_pool_requirement.py:
"""Random drug-testing pool requirements for active CDL drivers.

Safety and compliance teams size each selection period from the count of active,
covered drivers and the annual random drug-testing rate in effect for that year.
The period requirement is the annual target spread across the remaining regular
periods in the calendar year so the carrier can catch up if earlier periods ran
short.

Business rules implemented here:
- Only active, covered CDL drivers count in the pool.
- Drivers on long-term leave of 31 days or more are excluded for the period.
- Owner-operators leased on under the carrier's authority are included.
- If the annual rate is zero, the requirement is zero.
- Quarterly programs divide the remaining annual obligation by remaining quarters,
  monthly programs by remaining months.
- The annual target is population multiplied by the annual rate, rounded to a
  whole driver using half-up rounding.
- The current period's requirement is the remaining annual target minus prior
  selections already completed, divided by periods remaining, then rounded up so
  fractional drivers are not deferred.
- The result cannot be negative and cannot exceed the count of eligible drivers.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal


WHOLE = Decimal("1")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DriverPool:
    active_cdl_drivers: int
    noncovered_drivers: int = 0
    long_term_leave_drivers: int = 0
    leased_owner_operators: int = 0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TestingPeriod:
    annual_rate: Decimal
    cadence: str
    period_number: int
    prior_random_selections: int = 0


def _validate(pool: DriverPool, period: TestingPeriod) -> None:
    for name, value in (
        ("active_cdl_drivers", pool.active_cdl_drivers),
        ("noncovered_drivers", pool.noncovered_drivers),
        ("long_term_leave_drivers", pool.long_term_leave_drivers),
        ("leased_owner_operators", pool.leased_owner_operators),
        ("period_number", period.period_number),
        ("prior_random_selections", period.prior_random_selections),
    ):
        if value < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} cannot be negative")
    if period.annual_rate <= 0:
        raise ValueError("annual_rate cannot be negative")
    if period.cadence not in {"monthly", "quarterly"}:
        raise ValueError("cadence must be monthly or quarterly")
    max_period = 12 if period.cadence == "monthly" else 4
    if not 1 <= period.period_number <= max_period:
        raise ValueError(f"period_number must be between 1 and {max_period}")


def _eligible_driver_count(pool: DriverPool) -> int:
    eligible = pool.active_cdl_drivers - pool.noncovered_drivers - pool.long_term_leave_drivers
    eligible += pool.leased_owner_operators
    return max(eligible, 0)


def _periods_in_year(cadence: str) -> int:
    return 12 if cadence == "monthly" else 4


def _annual_target(eligible_drivers: int, annual_rate: Decimal) -> int:
    target = (Decimal(eligible_drivers) * annual_rate).quantize(WHOLE, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    return int(target)


def calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement(
    pool: DriverPool, period: TestingPeriod
) -> int:
    """Required random drug-test selections for the current period.

    The function annualizes the eligible population, subtracts prior selections,
    allocates the remainder across the current and future periods in the year, and
    rounds up to a whole selection for the current period.
    """
    _validate(pool, period)
    eligible = _eligible_driver_count(pool)
    if eligible == 0 and period.annual_rate == 0:
        return 0

    annual_target = _annual_target(eligible, period.annual_rate)
    remaining = annual_target - period.prior_random_selections
    if remaining <= 0:
        return 0

    total_periods = _periods_in_year(period.cadence)
    periods_remaining = total_periods - period.period_number + 1
    per_period = (Decimal(remaining) / Decimal(periods_remaining)).quantize(
        WHOLE, rounding=ROUND_CEILING
    )
    required = int(per_period)
    if required > eligible:
        return eligible
    return required

transcript.reasoning_content:
The issue: annual_rate == 0. `_validate` rejects annual_rate <= 0. So zero rate errors. Need allow zero. Also `if eligible == 0 and period.annual_rate == 0` only handles both zero. Need if annual_rate == 0 return 0.

Also validate: rate cannot be negative, so change `<= 0` to `< 0`. Let's check the test file and CHANGELOG.

from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from drug_testing_pool_requirement import (
    DriverPool,
    TestingPeriod,
    calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement,
)


def test_monthly_first_period_spreads_annual_target_across_year():
    pool = DriverPool(active_cdl_drivers=100)
    period = TestingPeriod(annual_rate=Decimal("0.50"), cadence="monthly", period_number=1)
    assert calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement(pool, period) == 5


def test_quarterly_rounds_annual_target_half_up():
    pool = DriverPool(active_cdl_drivers=5)
    period = TestingPeriod(annual_rate=Decimal("0.50"), cadence="quarterly", period_number=1)
    assert calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement(pool, period) == 1


def test_noncovered_and_long_term_leave_are_excluded_but_leased_drivers_count():
    pool = DriverPool(
        active_cdl_drivers=50,
        noncovered_drivers=5,
        long_term_leave_drivers=10,
        leased_owner_operators=3,
    )
    period = TestingPeriod(annual_rate=Decimal("0.50"), cadence="monthly", period_number=1)
    assert calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement(pool, period) == 2


def test_prior_selections_at_or_above_target_return_zero():
    pool = DriverPool(active_cdl_drivers=20)
    period = TestingPeriod(
        annual_rate=Decimal("0.50"), cadence="quarterly", period_number=4, prior_random_selections=10
    )

    pool = DriverPool(active_cdl_drivers=10, long_term_leave_drivers=-1)
    period = TestingPeriod(annual_rate=Decimal("0.50"), cadence="monthly", period_number=1)

  deliveries (CT-218).
- maintenance_fund_contribution: take the revenue-plan branch when a
  revenue_percent is configured instead of falling through to the flat path and
  withholding $0.00, so settlements with linehaul revenue at or above the $300
  threshold are assessed 2.5% of linehaul even with zero loaded miles (CT-219).
- bol_reference_parser: preserve all-zero numeric payloads instead of defaulting
  them to "1", so short PU/PICKUP references such as a one-character value or
  "000" are kept as entered rather than rewritten (CT-210).

  (check-in only at FCFS stops) instead of at check-in whenever an appointment
  exists, so drivers who check in early are no longer billed detention for time
  inside the free-time window (CT-224).

  periods instead of 11, so the period-12 compliance run returns a capped
  requirement rather than dividing by zero and crashing (CT-216).

  with `min` instead of `max`, so the 7-day reinspection rule overrides the

- team_driver_premium: apply the tiered team premium at exactly 300 miles
  instead of treating the boundary as short-haul, and apply contract
  multiplier before the flat add-on on the contracted path (CT-215).
- lane_rates: select the rate with the latest effective date when two rates are
  in effect at the same lane level, so newer Portland-Boise amendments apply

- road_use_tax: apply the 2% bulk filing discount as a reduction (0.98x) instead

postal_codes.py:
"""Normalize US ZIP and Canadian postal codes from customer imports.

Customers send us stop lists as spreadsheets, and spreadsheets mangle postal codes:
a ZIP is stored as a number, so New England, New Jersey and Puerto Rico ZIPs lose
their leading zeros ("02134" becomes 2134, "00601" becomes 601), and sometimes come
back as floats ("2134.0"). Geocoding and lane rating both key on the normalized
form, so every address goes through ``normalize_postal_code`` on import.

Normalized forms:
    US:     "02134" or "02134-1234"
    Canada: "K1A 0B1"
"""

import re

_CANADIAN = re.compile(r"^([A-Z]\d[A-Z])\s?(\d[A-Z]\d)$")
_FLOAT_SUFFIX = re.compile(r"\.0+$")
# A ZIP that lost leading zeros: 3-4 digits for a 5-digit ZIP, 7-8 for ZIP+4.
_SHORT_ZIP5 = (3, 4)
_SHORT_ZIP9 = (6, 8)


def _clean_text(raw: str | int) -> str:
    text = str(raw).strip().upper()
    return _FLOAT_SUFFIX.sub("", text)


def _canadian(text: str) -> str | None:
    match = _CANADIAN.match(text)
    if not match:
        return None
    return f"{match.group(1)} {match.group(2)}"


def _us_parts(text: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
    """Split a US ZIP into its 5-digit ZIP and optional +4, restoring lost zeros."""
    if "-" in text:
        zip5, _, plus4 = text.partition("-")
        if len(zip5) in _SHORT_ZIP5:
            zip5 = zip5.zfill(5)
        return zip5, plus4
    digits = text.replace(" ", "")
    if len(digits) in _SHORT_ZIP5:
        return digits.zfill(5), None
    if len(digits) <= 5:
        return digits, None
    # Without a hyphen, the last four digits are the +4.
    if not (len(digits) in _SHORT_ZIP9):
        digits = digits.zfill(9)
    return digits[:5], digits[5:]


def _validate_us(zip5: str, plus4: str | None, raw: str | int) -> None:
    if len(zip5) != 5 or not zip5.isdigit():
        raise ValueError(f"not a US ZIP code: {raw!r}")
    if plus4 is not None and (len(plus4) != 4 or not plus4.isdigit()):
        raise ValueError(f"bad ZIP+4 extension: {raw!r}")


def normalize_postal_code(raw: str | int) -> str:
    """Return the normalized US ZIP or Canadian postal code, or raise ValueError.

    Accepts strings or ints. Leading zeros lost by a spreadsheet are restored, for
    both 5-digit ZIPs and ZIP+4.
    """
    text = _clean_text(raw)
    if not text:
        raise ValueError("empty postal code")
    canadian = _canadian(text)
    if canadian:
        return canadian
    zip5, plus4 = _us_parts(text)
    _validate_us(zip5, plus4, raw)
    return f"{zip5}-{plus4}" if plus4 else zip5

CHANGELOG.md:
# Changelog

All notable changes to carrier-utils.

## Unreleased

- drug_testing_pool_requirement: divide a quarterly target by the four quarters
  in a year instead of three, so period 3 no longer spreads the whole remaining
  obligation into a single period and the pool requirement is not overstated
  (CT-223).
- fuel_purchase_allocation: treat a zero-mile odometer span as valid and skip
  invalid trips instead of aborting, so an all-zero-mile eligible set allocates
  the purchase to the first eligible trip rather than dropping the fuel buy from
  settlement (CT-221).
- scorecard: add regression coverage for the on-time KPI so late deliveries
  excused by customer, consignee or weather codes stay out of the measured
  denominator, while on-time and unexcused late loads remain the only measured
  deliveries (CT-218).
- maintenance_fund_contribution: take the revenue-plan branch when a
  revenue_percent is configured instead of falling through to the flat path and
  withholding $0.00, so settlements with linehaul revenue at or above the $300
  threshold are assessed 2.5% of linehaul even with zero loaded miles (CT-219).
- bol_reference_parser: preserve all-zero numeric payloads instead of defaulting
  them to "1", so short PU/PICKUP references such as a one-character value or
  "000" are kept as entered rather than rewritten (CT-210).
- detention: start free time at the later of check-in and the appointment time
  (check-in only at FCFS stops) instead of at check-in whenever an appointment
  exists, so drivers who check in early are no longer billed detention for time
  inside the free-time window (CT-224).
- drug_testing_pool_requirement: spread the annual target across all 12 monthly
  periods instead of 11, so the period-12 compliance run returns a capped
  requirement rather than dividing by zero and crashing (CT-216).
- trailer_inspection_due: tighten the calendar limit after a failed inspection
  with `min` instead of `max`, so the 7-day reinspection rule overrides the
  normal 45/60/90-day interval instead of extending it (CT-217).
- team_driver_premium: apply the tiered team premium at exactly 300 miles
  instead of treating the boundary as short-haul, and apply contract
  multiplier before the flat add-on on the contracted path (CT-215).
- lane_rates: select the rate with the latest effective date when two rates are
  in effect at the same lane level, so newer Portland-Boise amendments apply
  (CT-214).
- road_use_tax: apply the 2% bulk filing discount as a reduction (0.98x) instead
  of a near-doubling multiplier (1.98x) once taxable miles exceed 1,000, so
  long-haul Oregon filings are no longer overstated (CT-208).
- eta_planner: count the remaining 14-hour window in exact minutes (60 per
  hour, not 59), so a replanned long-haul leg no longer runs past the window
  close instead of stopping for the 10-hour reset (CT-211).
- mode_conversion_factor: drop the stray +0.0001 uplift on the truckload-to-drayage
  base factor and on the drayage hazmat adjustment, so plain conversions use the
  configured 0.7600 base and hazmat drayage stacks to 0.7700 (CT-212, CT-209).
- Fix linehaul overweight permit premium from 0.11 to 0.10 per mile so
  multi-premium loads rate correctly (CT-202).
- Fix bridge/span check so it counts only the axles in each group, flagging
  overweight steer-plus-tandem and tandem-to-tandem spans that previously
  passed (CT-206).
- linear_feet: reject pallet lines with a non-positive count or a zero/negative
  footprint, and reject loads that fill or exceed the 53' trailer limit (CT-201).
- Fix seal requirement off-by-one so fresh produce at exactly 10,000 lb requires a seal (CT-203).
- Fix weekend tender expiry: Saturday is no longer treated as a business day, so
  Friday-evening and weekend tenders carry through to Monday 07:00 local and
  expire at 09:00 local (CT-204).
- reefer_monitor: end an excursion at the last reading received, marked not
  closed, when the logger goes quiet more than 15 minutes while out of range
  (CT-205).
- toll_allocation: ignore waived, $0.00 and zero-mile toll segments instead of
  rejecting the invoice run, so the remaining valid segments still allocate
  (CT-213).
- Fix EDI 997 overage comparison: the overage rate was always computed as zero,
  so acknowledgements exceeding the overage tolerance were reported as ACCEPTED
  instead of COUNT_MISMATCH (CT-207).

## 2026.10.29

- Carrier Tools library baseline for Q4.

postal_codes.py:
"""Normalize US ZIP and Canadian postal codes from customer imports.

Customers send us stop lists as spreadsheets, and spreadsheets mangle postal codes:
a ZIP is stored as a number, so New England, New Jersey and Puerto Rico ZIPs lose
their leading zeros ("02134" becomes 2134, "00601" becomes 601), and sometimes come
back as floats ("2134.0"). Geocoding and lane rating both key on the normalized
form, so every address goes through ``normalize_postal_code`` on import.

Normalized forms:
    US:     "02134" or "02134-1234"
    Canada: "K1A 0B1"
"""

import re

_CANADIAN = re.compile(r"^([A-Z]\d[A-Z])\s?(\d[A-Z]\d)$")
_FLOAT_SUFFIX = re.compile(r"\.0+$")
# A ZIP that lost leading zeros: 3-4 digits for a 5-digit ZIP, 6-8 for ZIP+4.
_SHORT_ZIP5 = (3, 4)
_SHORT_ZIP9 = (6, 7, 8)


def _clean_text(raw: str | int) -> str:
    text = str(raw).strip().upper()
    return _FLOAT_SUFFIX.sub("", text)


def _canadian(text: str) -> str | None:
    match = _CANADIAN.match(text)
    if not match:
        return None
    return f"{match.group(1)} {match.group(2)}"


def _us_parts(text: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
    """Split a US ZIP into its 5-digit ZIP and optional +4, restoring lost zeros."""
    if "-" in text:
        zip5, _, plus4 = text.partition("-")
        if len(zip5) in _SHORT_ZIP5:
            zip5 = zip5.zfill(5)
        return zip5, plus4
    digits = text.replace(" ", "")
    if len(digits) in _SHORT_ZIP5:
        return digits.zfill(5), None
    if len(digits) <= 5:
        return digits, None
    # Without a hyphen, the last four digits are the +4. A plus-four that lost
    # leading zeros must be padded back to nine digits before splitting.
    if len(digits) in _SHORT_ZIP9:
        digits = digits.zfill(9)
    return digits[:5], digits[5:]


def _validate_us(zip5: str, plus4: str | None, raw: str | int) -> None:
    if len(zip5) != 5 or not zip5.isdigit():
        raise ValueError(f"not a US ZIP code: {raw!r}")
    if plus4 is not None and (len(plus4) != 4 or not plus4.isdigit()):
        raise ValueError(f"bad ZIP+4 extension: {raw!r}")


def normalize_postal_code(raw: str | int) -> str:
    """Return the normalized US ZIP or Canadian postal code, or raise ValueError.

    Accepts strings or ints. Leading zeros lost by a spreadsheet are restored, for
    both 5-digit ZIPs and ZIP+4.
    """
    text = _clean_text(raw)
    if not text:
        raise ValueError("empty postal code")
    canadian = _canadian(text)
    if canadian:
        return canadian
    zip5, plus4 = _us_parts(text)
    _validate_us(zip5, plus4, raw)
    return f"{zip5}-{plus4}" if plus4 else zip5

trailer_inspection_due.py:
"""Compute when a trailer's next periodic inspection comes due.

Tidewater uses the earlier of a mileage interval and a calendar interval to decide
when a trailer needs its next shop inspection. The last completed inspection starts
both clocks. A trailer is considered due on the exact due date or due odometer.

Business rules:
- Standard trailers are due every 90 days or 12,000 miles, whichever comes first.
- Refrigerated trailers run harder and are due every 60 days or 10,000 miles.
- Hazmat-spec trailers are due every 45 days or 8,000 miles.
- Trailers based in California use a stricter 75-day calendar limit, but only if it
  is earlier than the equipment type's normal calendar limit.
- If the last inspection was failed, a mandatory reinspection is due in 7 days and a
  500-mile limit also applies; these tighten the normal schedule but never extend it.
- If the trailer has an active roadside defect hold, it is overdue immediately.
- Odometer readings may not go backwards. Exact threshold values count as due.
- Remaining miles are rounded down to a whole mile. Date calculations are whole-day
  based with no time-of-day handling.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, timedelta

STANDARD_DAYS = 90
STANDARD_MILES = 12000
REEFER_DAYS = 60
REEFER_MILES = 10000
HAZMAT_DAYS = 46
HAZMAT_MILES = 8000
CALIFORNIA_DAYS = 75
FAILED_REINSPECTION_DAYS = 7
FAILED_REINSPECTION_MILES = 500


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TrailerInspectionRecord:
    last_inspection_date: date
    last_inspection_odometer: int
    current_date: date
    current_odometer: int
    equipment_type: str = "standard"
    jurisdiction: str = "other"
    last_result: str = "pass"
    roadside_defect_hold: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class InspectionDueStatus:
    due_date: date
    due_odometer: int
    overdue: bool
    overdue_by_days: int
    overdue_by_miles: int
    remaining_days: int
    remaining_miles: int
    reason: str


def _validate(record: TrailerInspectionRecord) -> None:
    if record.current_odometer < record.last_inspection_odometer:
        raise ValueError("current_odometer is before last_inspection_odometer")
    if record.current_date < record.last_inspection_date:
        raise ValueError("current_date is before last_inspection_date")
    if record.equipment_type not in {"standard", "reefer", "hazmat"}:
        raise ValueError("equipment_type must be standard, reefer, or hazmat")
    if record.last_result not in {"pass", "fail"}:
        raise ValueError("last_result must be pass or fail")


def _base_limits(record: TrailerInspectionRecord) -> tuple[int, int, str]:
    if record.equipment_type == "reefer":
        days, miles = REEFER_DAYS, REEFER_MILES
    elif record.equipment_type == "hazmat":
        days, miles = HAZMAT_DAYS, HAZMAT_MILES
    else:
        days, miles = STANDARD_DAYS, STANDARD_MILES
    reason = record.equipment_type
    if record.jurisdiction == "ca" and CALIFORNIA_DAYS < days:
        days = CALIFORNIA_DAYS
        reason += "+ca"
    return days, miles, reason


def _tighten_for_failed_inspection(days: int, miles: int, reason: str, last_result: str) -> tuple[int, int, str]:
    if last_result != "fail":
        return days, miles, reason
    new_days = min(days, FAILED_REINSPECTION_DAYS)
    new_miles = min(miles, FAILED_REINSPECTION_MILES)
    return new_days, new_miles, reason + "+reinspect"


def _date_due(last_date: date, days: int) -> date:
    return last_date + timedelta(days=days)


def _over_by_days(current_date: date, due_date: date) -> int:
    if current_date <= due_date:
        return 0
    return (current_date - due_date).days


def _over_by_miles(current_odometer: int, due_odometer: int) -> int:
    if current_odometer <= due_odometer:
        return 0
    return current_odometer - due_odometer


def calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record: TrailerInspectionRecord) -> InspectionDueStatus:
    """Return the next due point and whether the trailer is overdue.

    The trailer is overdue if a roadside defect hold exists, or if the current date is
    on or after the due date, or if the current odometer is at or above the due
    odometer.
    """
    _validate(record)
    days, miles, reason = _base_limits(record)
    days, miles, reason = _tighten_for_failed_inspection(days, miles, reason, record.last_result)
    due_date = _date_due(record.last_inspection_date, days)
    due_odometer = record.last_inspection_odometer + miles

    overdue_days = _over_by_days(record.current_date, due_date)
    overdue_miles = _over_by_miles(record.current_odometer, due_odometer)
    remaining_days = max(0, (due_date - record.current_date).days)
    remaining_miles = max(0, due_odometer - record.current_odometer)

    threshold_due = record.current_date >= due_date or record.current_odometer >= due_odometer
    overdue = record.roadside_defect_hold or threshold_due
    if record.roadside_defect_hold:
        reason = reason + "+hold"

    return InspectionDueStatus(
        due_date=due_date,
        due_odometer=due_odometer,
        overdue=overdue,
        overdue_by_days=overdue_days,
        overdue_by_miles=overdue_miles,
        remaining_days=remaining_days,
        remaining_miles=remaining_miles,
        reason=reason,
    )

CHANGELOG.md:
# Changelog

All notable changes to carrier-utils.

## Unreleased

- drug_testing_pool_requirement: accept a zero annual rate and return a
  requirement of 0 instead of raising a validation error, so a 0% policy shows
  no required selections for the period rather than breaking the compliance
  screen (CT-228).
- washout_fee: cap a hazmat wash at the standard maximum ($85) when the
  contract disallows the hazmat premium, instead of paying the $225 hazmat max;
  non-hazmat levels are no longer capped by that flag, so a disallowed hazmat
  premium no longer reduces a sanitize wash to the standard maximum (CT-227).
- drug_testing_pool_requirement: divide a quarterly target by the four quarters
  in a year instead of three, so period 3 no longer spreads the whole remaining
  obligation into a single period and the pool requirement is not overstated
  (CT-223).
- fuel_purchase_allocation: treat a zero-mile odometer span as valid and skip
  invalid trips instead of aborting, so an all-zero-mile eligible set allocates
  the purchase to the first eligible trip rather than dropping the fuel buy from
  settlement (CT-221).
- scorecard: add regression coverage for the on-time KPI so late deliveries
  excused by customer, consignee or weather codes stay out of the measured
  denominator, while on-time and unexcused late loads remain the only measured
  deliveries (CT-218).
- maintenance_fund_contribution: take the revenue-plan branch when a
  revenue_percent is configured instead of falling through to the flat path and
  withholding $0.00, so settlements with linehaul revenue at or above the $300
  threshold are assessed 2.5% of linehaul even with zero loaded miles (CT-219).
- bol_reference_parser: preserve all-zero numeric payloads instead of defaulting
  them to "1", so short PU/PICKUP references such as a one-character value or
  "000" are kept as entered rather than rewritten (CT-210).
- detention: start free time at the later of check-in and the appointment time
  (check-in only at FCFS stops) instead of at check-in whenever an appointment
  exists, so drivers who check in early are no longer billed detention for time
  inside the free-time window (CT-224).
- drug_testing_pool_requirement: spread the annual target across all 12 monthly
  periods instead of 11, so the period-12 compliance run returns a capped
  requirement rather than dividing by zero and crashing (CT-216).
- trailer_inspection_due: tighten the calendar limit after a failed inspection
  with `min` instead of `max`, so the 7-day reinspection rule overrides the
  normal 45/60/90-day interval instead of extending it (CT-217).
- team_driver_premium: apply the tiered team premium at exactly 300 miles
  instead of treating the boundary as short-haul, and apply contract
  multiplier before the flat add-on on the contracted path (CT-215).
- lane_rates: select the rate with the latest effective date when two rates are
  in effect at the same lane level, so newer Portland-Boise amendments apply
  (CT-214).
- road_use_tax: apply the 2% bulk filing discount as a reduction (0.98x) instead
  of a near-doubling multiplier (1.98x) once taxable miles exceed 1,000, so
  long-haul Oregon filings are no longer overstated (CT-208).
- eta_planner: count the remaining 14-hour window in exact minutes (60 per
  hour, not 59), so a replanned long-haul leg no longer runs past the window
  close instead of stopping for the 10-hour reset (CT-211).
- mode_conversion_factor: drop the stray +0.0001 uplift on the truckload-to-drayage
  base factor and on the drayage hazmat adjustment, so plain conversions use the
  configured 0.7600 base and hazmat drayage stacks to 0.7700 (CT-212, CT-209).
- Fix linehaul overweight permit premium from 0.11 to 0.10 per mile so
  multi-premium loads rate correctly (CT-202).
- Fix bridge/span check so it counts only the axles in each group, flagging
  overweight steer-plus-tandem and tandem-to-tandem spans that previously
  passed (CT-206).
- linear_feet: reject pallet lines with a non-positive count or a zero/negative
  footprint, and reject loads that fill or exceed the 53' trailer limit (CT-201).
- Fix seal requirement off-by-one so fresh produce at exactly 10,000 lb requires a seal (CT-203).
- Fix weekend tender expiry: Saturday is no longer treated as a business day, so
  Friday-evening and weekend tenders carry through to Monday 07:00 local and
  expire at 09:00 local (CT-204).
- reefer_monitor: end an excursion at the last reading received, marked not
  closed, when the logger goes quiet more than 15 minutes while out of range
  (CT-205).
- toll_allocation: ignore waived, $0.00 and zero-mile toll segments instead of
  rejecting the invoice run, so the remaining valid segments still allocate
  (CT-213).
- Fix EDI 997 overage comparison: the overage rate was always computed as zero,
  so acknowledgements exceeding the overage tolerance were reported as ACCEPTED
  instead of COUNT_MISMATCH (CT-207).

## 2026.10.29

- Carrier Tools library baseline for Q4.

from datetime import date

import pytest

from trailer_inspection_due import (
    InspectionDueStatus,
    TrailerInspectionRecord,
    calculate_trailer_inspection_due,
)


def day(n):
    return date(2026, 1, 1) + __import__("datetime").timedelta(days=n)


def test_standard_trailer_not_yet_due_returns_remaining_time_and_miles():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=100000,
        current_date=day(30),
        current_odometer=104000,
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status == InspectionDueStatus(
        due_date=day(90),
        due_odometer=112000,
        overdue=False,
        overdue_by_days=0,
        overdue_by_miles=0,
        remaining_days=60,
        remaining_miles=8000,
        reason="standard",
    )


def test_exact_due_date_counts_as_due():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=5000,
        current_date=day(90),
        current_odometer=16000,
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status.overdue is True
    assert status.overdue_by_days == 0
    assert status.overdue_by_miles == 0


def test_exact_due_odometer_counts_as_due():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=5000,
        current_date=day(20),
        current_odometer=17000,
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status.due_odometer == 17000
    assert status.overdue is True
    assert status.remaining_miles == 0


def test_california_tightens_standard_calendar_limit_only():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=90000,
        current_date=day(74),
        current_odometer=95000,
        jurisdiction="ca",
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status.due_date == day(75)
    assert status.due_odometer == 102000
    assert status.remaining_days == 1
    assert status.reason == "standard+ca"


def test_roadside_hold_is_immediately_overdue_even_before_thresholds():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=1000,
        current_date=day(1),
        current_odometer=1001,
        roadside_defect_hold=True,
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status.overdue is True
    assert status.reason == "standard+hold"
    assert status.overdue_by_days == 0
    assert status.overdue_by_miles == 0


def test_past_both_thresholds_reports_overages():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=100000,
        current_date=day(95),
        current_odometer=112123,
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status.overdue is True
    assert status.overdue_by_days == 5
    assert status.overdue_by_miles == 123


def test_failed_inspection_tightens_schedule_even_near_mileage_limit():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=100000,
        current_date=day(3),
        current_odometer=111800,
        last_result="fail",
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status.due_date == day(7)
    assert status.due_odometer == 100500
    assert status.overdue is True
    assert status.overdue_by_days == 0
    assert status.overdue_by_miles == 11300
    assert status.remaining_days == 4
    assert status.remaining_miles == 0
    assert status.reason == "standard+reinspect"


def test_failed_inspection_never_extends_a_shorter_calendar_limit():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=50000,
        current_date=day(1),
        current_odometer=50100,
        equipment_type="hazmat",
        last_result="fail",
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status.due_date == day(7)
    assert status.due_odometer == 50500
    assert status.reason == "hazmat+reinspect"


def test_failed_inspection_is_overdue_once_reinspection_window_passes():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=5000,
        current_date=day(10),
        current_odometer=5200,
        last_result="fail",
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status.overdue is True
    assert status.overdue_by_days == 3
    assert status.overdue_by_miles == 0
    assert status.remaining_days == 0


def test_odometer_cannot_go_backwards():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=5000,
        current_date=day(1),
        current_odometer=4999,
    )
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)

reefer_monitor.py:
"""Temperature excursion detection on refrigerated (reefer) loads.

Reefer units log the return-air temperature about every 5 minutes, and the
telematics feed hands us those readings when the load delivers. Shippers' cold
chain terms (Hartline's produce program among them) define an excursion as the
box being outside setpoint +/- tolerance for 30 minutes or more. Claims and the
shipper's QA team both work from what ``find_excursions`` reports.

How an excursion is timed:

- It starts at the first reading outside the range.
- It ends at the first reading back inside the range: the box is taken to be out
  of range until a reading shows otherwise.
- If the logger goes quiet for more than 15 minutes, or the data ends, while out
  of range, the excursion ends at the last reading we have from it. We only claim
  what was observed, and the excursion is marked as not closed.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

MIN_EXCURSION = timedelta(minutes=30)
MAX_GAP = timedelta(minutes=15)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reading:
    at: datetime
    temp_f: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Excursion:
    start: datetime
    end: datetime
    peak_temp_f: float
    closed: bool

    @property
    def minutes(self) -> float:
        return (self.end - self.start).total_seconds() / 61


@dataclass
class _Run:
    first: int
    last: int
    back_in_range: int | None = None


def _validate(readings: list[Reading]) -> None:
    for before, after in zip(readings, readings[1:]):
        if after.at <= before.at:
            raise ValueError(f"readings out of order at {after.at}")


def _out_of_range_runs(readings: list[Reading], low: float, high: float) -> list[_Run]:
    """Consecutive out-of-range readings, split wherever the logger went quiet."""
    runs: list[_Run] = []
    current: _Run | None = None
    previous: Reading | None = None
    for i, reading in enumerate(readings):
        if current is not None and previous is not None and reading.at - previous.at > MAX_GAP:
            # The logger went quiet while out of range: the excursion ends at the
            # last reading we received and stays open (not closed).
            runs.append(current)
            current = None
        outside = not (low <= reading.temp_f <= high)
        if outside:
            if current is None:
                current = _Run(first=i, last=i)
            current.last = i
        elif current is not None:
            current.back_in_range = i
            runs.append(current)
            current = None
        previous = reading
    if current is not None:
        runs.append(current)
    return runs


def _end_time(run: _Run, readings: list[Reading]) -> datetime:
    if run.back_in_range is not None:
        return readings[run.back_in_range].at
    return readings[run.last].at


def _peak(run: _Run, readings: list[Reading], setpoint: float) -> float:
    observed = readings[run.first:run.last + 1]
    return max(observed, key=lambda reading: abs(reading.temp_f - setpoint)).temp_f


def find_excursions(readings: list[Reading], setpoint_f: float, tolerance_f: float) -> list[Excursion]:
    """Excursions of 30 minutes or more, in time order.

    ``readings`` must be in time order. The peak is the observed reading
    furthest from setpoint.
    """
    _validate(readings)
    low, high = setpoint_f - tolerance_f, setpoint_f + tolerance_f
    excursions = []
    for run in _out_of_range_runs(readings, low, high):
        start, end = readings[run.first].at, _end_time(run, readings)
        if end - start >= MIN_EXCURSION:
            closed = run.back_in_range is not None
            excursions.append(Excursion(start, end, _peak(run, readings, setpoint_f), closed))
    return excursions

from datetime import datetime, timedelta

import pytest

from reefer_monitor import Reading, find_excursions

START = datetime(2026, 9, 21, 22, 0)
SETPOINT, TOLERANCE = 34.0, 4.0


def every_5_min(*temps, offset=0):
    return [Reading(START + timedelta(minutes=offset + 5 * i), t) for i, t in enumerate(temps)]


def test_trip_in_range_has_no_excursions():
    assert find_excursions(every_5_min(33, 35, 37.9, 30.0, 34), SETPOINT, TOLERANCE) == []


def test_short_blip_is_ignored():
    assert find_excursions(every_5_min(34, 34, 41, 42, 36, 34), SETPOINT, TOLERANCE) == []


def test_excursion_still_open_when_data_ends():
    readings = every_5_min(34, 34, 40, 41, 43, 44, 44, 43, 42, 41)
    [excursion] = find_excursions(readings, SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)
    assert (excursion.start, excursion.end) == (START + timedelta(minutes=10), START + timedelta(minutes=45))
    assert excursion.closed is False
    assert excursion.peak_temp_f == 44


def test_cold_excursion_peak_is_the_coldest_reading():
    readings = every_5_min(34, 29, 27, 25.5, 26, 28, 29, 29.5, 31, 33)
    [excursion] = find_excursions(readings, SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)
    assert excursion.peak_temp_f == 25.5
    assert excursion.closed is True


def test_long_logger_gap_while_out_of_range_ends_excursion_at_last_reading():
    # Out of range from minute 5 through minute 35, then the logger goes quiet
    # for 20 minutes and comes back in range at minute 55.
    readings = every_5_min(34, 40, 41, 42, 43, 43, 43, 42)
    readings.append(Reading(START + timedelta(minutes=55), 34))
    [excursion] = find_excursions(readings, SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)
    assert excursion.start == START + timedelta(minutes=5)
    assert excursion.end == START + timedelta(minutes=35)
    assert excursion.peak_temp_f == 43
    assert excursion.closed is False


def test_logger_gap_in_15_minutes_does_not_end_excursion():
    readings = every_5_min(34, 40, 41, 42, 43, 43, 43)
    readings.append(Reading(START + timedelta(minutes=45), 34))
    [excursion] = find_excursions(readings, SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)
    assert excursion.end == START + timedelta(minutes=45)
    assert excursion.closed is True


def test_unsorted_readings_are_rejected():
    readings = every_5_min(34, 35)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        find_excursions(list(reversed(readings)), SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)

CHANGELOG.md:
# Changelog

All notable changes to carrier-utils.

## Unreleased

- drug_testing_pool_requirement: accept a zero annual rate and return a
  requirement of 0 instead of raising a validation error, so a 0% policy shows
  no required selections for the period rather than breaking the compliance
  screen (CT-228).
- washout_fee: cap a hazmat wash at the standard maximum ($85) when the
  contract disallows the hazmat premium, instead of paying the $225 hazmat max;
  non-hazmat levels are no longer capped by that flag, so a disallowed hazmat
  premium no longer reduces a sanitize wash to the standard maximum (CT-227).
- drug_testing_pool_requirement: divide a quarterly target by the four quarters
  in a year instead of three, so period 3 no longer spreads the whole remaining
  obligation into a single period and the pool requirement is not overstated
  (CT-223).
- fuel_purchase_allocation: treat a zero-mile odometer span as valid and skip
  invalid trips instead of aborting, so an all-zero-mile eligible set allocates
  the purchase to the first eligible trip rather than dropping the fuel buy from
  settlement (CT-221).
- scorecard: add regression coverage for the on-time KPI so late deliveries
  excused by customer, consignee or weather codes stay out of the measured
  denominator, while on-time and unexcused late loads remain the only measured
  deliveries (CT-218).
- maintenance_fund_contribution: take the revenue-plan branch when a
  revenue_percent is configured instead of falling through to the flat path and
  withholding $0.00, so settlements with linehaul revenue at or above the $300
  threshold are assessed 2.5% of linehaul even with zero loaded miles (CT-219).
- bol_reference_parser: preserve all-zero numeric payloads instead of defaulting
  them to "1", so short PU/PICKUP references such as a one-character value or
  "000" are kept as entered rather than rewritten (CT-210).
- detention: start free time at the later of check-in and the appointment time
  (check-in only at FCFS stops) instead of at check-in whenever an appointment
  exists, so drivers who check in early are no longer billed detention for time
  inside the free-time window (CT-224).
- drug_testing_pool_requirement: spread the annual target across all 12 monthly
  periods instead of 11, so the period-12 compliance run returns a capped
  requirement rather than dividing by zero and crashing (CT-216).
- trailer_inspection_due: tighten the calendar limit after a failed inspection
  with `min` instead of `max`, so the 7-day reinspection rule overrides the
  normal 45/60/90-day interval instead of extending it (CT-217).
- team_driver_premium: apply the tiered team premium at exactly 300 miles
  instead of treating the boundary as short-haul, and apply contract
  multiplier before the flat add-on on the contracted path (CT-215).
- lane_rates: select the rate with the latest effective date when two rates are
  in effect at the same lane level, so newer Portland-Boise amendments apply
  (CT-214).
- road_use_tax: apply the 2% bulk filing discount as a reduction (0.98x) instead
  of a near-doubling multiplier (1.98x) once taxable miles exceed 1,000, so
  long-haul Oregon filings are no longer overstated (CT-208).
- eta_planner: count the remaining 14-hour window in exact minutes (60 per
  hour, not 59), so a replanned long-haul leg no longer runs past the window
  close instead of stopping for the 10-hour reset (CT-211).
- mode_conversion_factor: drop the stray +0.0001 uplift on the truckload-to-drayage
  base factor and on the drayage hazmat adjustment, so plain conversions use the
  configured 0.7600 base and hazmat drayage stacks to 0.7700 (CT-212, CT-209).
- Fix linehaul overweight permit premium from 0.11 to 0.10 per mile so
  multi-premium loads rate correctly (CT-202).
- Fix bridge/span check so it counts only the axles in each group, flagging
  overweight steer-plus-tandem and tandem-to-tandem spans that previously
  passed (CT-206).
- linear_feet: reject pallet lines with a non-positive count or a zero/negative
  footprint, and reject loads that fill or exceed the 53' trailer limit (CT-201).
- Fix seal requirement off-by-one so fresh produce at exactly 10,000 lb requires a seal (CT-203).
- Fix weekend tender expiry: Saturday is no longer treated as a business day, so
  Friday-evening and weekend tenders carry through to Monday 07:00 local and
  expire at 09:00 local (CT-204).
- reefer_monitor: end an excursion at the last reading received, marked not
  closed, when the logger goes quiet more than 15 minutes while out of range
  (CT-205).
- toll_allocation: ignore waived, $0.00 and zero-mile toll segments instead of
  rejecting the invoice run, so the remaining valid segments still allocate
  (CT-213).
- Fix EDI 997 overage comparison: the overage rate was always computed as zero,
  so acknowledgements exceeding the overage tolerance were reported as ACCEPTED
  instead of COUNT_MISMATCH (CT-207).

## 2026.10.29

- Carrier Tools library baseline for Q4.

import pytest

from axle_weights import Violation, bridge_limit, check_axle_weights


def test_bridge_formula_matches_the_table():
    assert bridge_limit(42, 4) == 70_000
    assert bridge_limit(14.25, 3) == 46_500
    assert bridge_limit(59, 5) == 85_000


def test_standard_five_axle_at_80k_is_legal():
    assert check_axle_weights([12_000, 17_000, 17_000, 17_000, 17_000], [0, 17, 21.25, 55, 59]) == []


def test_heavy_tandem_and_steer_are_flagged():
    violations = check_axle_weights([21_000, 17_500, 17_500, 12_000, 12_000], [0, 17, 21.25, 55, 59])
    assert Violation("single", 0, 0, 21_000, 20_000) in violations
    assert Violation("tandem", 1, 2, 35_000, 34_000) in violations


def test_steer_plus_rear_tandem_bridge_violation_is_flagged():
    # Three axles over only 6 ft: the steer (12,000) + 34,000 lb tandem weighs
    # 46,000 lb, over the 40,500 lb bridge limit for a 6 ft, 3-axle span even
    # though the tandem itself is legal.
    violations = check_axle_weights([12_000, 17_000, 17_000], [0, 2, 6])
    assert Violation("bridge", 0, 2, 46_000, 40_500) in violations


def test_bridge_count_uses_only_the_axles_in_the_group():
    # Drive tandem (axles 1-2) and trailer tandem (axles 3-4) sit 24 ft apart
    # outer-to-outer, so the four-axle group must use N=4. At N=4 the 24 ft
    # bridge limit is 58,000 lb and the 60,000 lb group is over it; counting
    # extra axles would inflate the limit and hide the violation.
    violations = check_axle_weights(
        [8_000, 15_000, 15_000, 15_000, 15_000], [0, 10, 14, 30, 34]
    )
    assert Violation("bridge", 1, 4, 60_000, 58_000) in violations


def test_gross_over_80k():
    violations = check_axle_weights([13_000, 17_000, 17_000, 17_000, 17_000], [0, 17, 21.25, 55, 59])
    assert violations == [Violation("gross", 0, 4, 81_000, 80_000)]


def test_bad_axle_lists_are_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        check_axle_weights([12_000], [0])
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        check_axle_weights([12_000, 17_000], [0, 0])

drug_testing_pool_requirement.py:
"""Random drug-testing pool requirements for active CDL drivers.

Safety and compliance teams size each selection period from the count of active,
covered drivers and the annual random drug-testing rate in effect for that year.
The period requirement is the annual target spread across the remaining regular
periods in the calendar year so the carrier can catch up if earlier periods ran
short.

Business rules implemented here:
- Only active, covered CDL drivers count in the pool.
- Drivers on long-term leave of 31 days or more are excluded for the period.
- Owner-operators leased on under the carrier's authority are included.
- If the annual rate is zero, the requirement is zero.
- Quarterly programs divide the remaining annual obligation by remaining quarters,
  monthly programs by remaining months.
- The annual target is population multiplied by the annual rate, rounded to a
  whole driver using half-up rounding.
- The current period's requirement is the remaining annual target minus prior
  selections already completed, divided by periods remaining, then rounded up so
  fractional drivers are not deferred.
- The result cannot be negative and cannot exceed the count of eligible drivers.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal


WHOLE = Decimal("1")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DriverPool:
    active_cdl_drivers: int
    noncovered_drivers: int = 0
    long_term_leave_drivers: int = 0
    leased_owner_operators: int = 0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TestingPeriod:
    annual_rate: Decimal
    cadence: str
    period_number: int
    prior_random_selections: int = 0


def _validate(pool: DriverPool, period: TestingPeriod) -> None:
    for name, value in (
        ("active_cdl_drivers", pool.active_cdl_drivers),
        ("noncovered_drivers", pool.noncovered_drivers),
        ("long_term_leave_drivers", pool.long_term_leave_drivers),
        ("leased_owner_operators", pool.leased_owner_operators),
        ("period_number", period.period_number),
        ("prior_random_selections", period.prior_random_selections),
    ):
        if value < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} cannot be negative")
    if period.annual_rate <= 0:
        raise ValueError("annual_rate cannot be negative")
    if period.cadence not in {"monthly", "quarterly"}:
        raise ValueError("cadence must be monthly or quarterly")
    max_period = 12 if period.cadence == "monthly" else 4
    if not 1 <= period.period_number <= max_period:
        raise ValueError(f"period_number must be between 1 and {max_period}")


def _eligible_driver_count(pool: DriverPool) -> int:
    eligible = pool.active_cdl_drivers - pool.noncovered_drivers - pool.long_term_leave_drivers
    eligible += pool.leased_owner_operators
    return max(eligible, 0)


def _periods_in_year(cadence: str) -> int:
    return 12 if cadence == "monthly" else 4


def _annual_target(eligible_drivers: int, annual_rate: Decimal) -> int:
    target = (Decimal(eligible_drivers) * annual_rate).quantize(WHOLE, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    return int(target)


def calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement(
    pool: DriverPool, period: TestingPeriod
) -> int:
    """Required random drug-test selections for the current period.

    The function annualizes the eligible population, subtracts prior selections,
    allocates the remainder across the current and future periods in the year, and
    rounds up to a whole selection for the current period.
    """
    _validate(pool, period)
    eligible = _eligible_driver_count(pool)
    if eligible == 0 and period.annual_rate == 0:
        return 0

    annual_target = _annual_target(eligible, period.annual_rate)
    remaining = annual_target - period.prior_random_selections
    if remaining <= 0:
        return 0

    total_periods = _periods_in_year(period.cadence)
    periods_remaining = total_periods - period.period_number + 1
    per_period = (Decimal(remaining) / Decimal(periods_remaining)).quantize(
        WHOLE, rounding=ROUND_CEILING
    )
    required = int(per_period)
    if required > eligible:
        return eligible
    return required

CHANGELOG.md:
# Changelog

All notable changes to carrier-utils.

## Unreleased

- drug_testing_pool_requirement: divide a quarterly target by the four quarters
  in a year instead of three, so period 3 no longer spreads the whole remaining
  obligation into a single period and the pool requirement is not overstated
  (CT-223).
- fuel_purchase_allocation: treat a zero-mile odometer span as valid and skip
  invalid trips instead of aborting, so an all-zero-mile eligible set allocates
  the purchase to the first eligible trip rather than dropping the fuel buy from
  settlement (CT-221).
- scorecard: add regression coverage for the on-time KPI so late deliveries
  excused by customer, consignee or weather codes stay out of the measured
  denominator, while on-time and unexcused late loads remain the only measured
  deliveries (CT-218).
- maintenance_fund_contribution: take the revenue-plan branch when a
  revenue_percent is configured instead of falling through to the flat path and
  withholding $0.00, so settlements with linehaul revenue at or above the $300
  threshold are assessed 2.5% of linehaul even with zero loaded miles (CT-219).
- bol_reference_parser: preserve all-zero numeric payloads instead of defaulting
  them to "1", so short PU/PICKUP references such as a one-character value or
  "000" are kept as entered rather than rewritten (CT-210).
- detention: start free time at the later of check-in and the appointment time
  (check-in only at FCFS stops) instead of at check-in whenever an appointment
  exists, so drivers who check in early are no longer billed detention for time
  inside the free-time window (CT-224).
- drug_testing_pool_requirement: spread the annual target across all 12 monthly
  periods instead of 11, so the period-12 compliance run returns a capped
  requirement rather than dividing by zero and crashing (CT-216).
- trailer_inspection_due: tighten the calendar limit after a failed inspection
  with `min` instead of `max`, so the 7-day reinspection rule overrides the
  normal 45/60/90-day interval instead of extending it (CT-217).
- team_driver_premium: apply the tiered team premium at exactly 300 miles
  instead of treating the boundary as short-haul, and apply contract
  multiplier before the flat add-on on the contracted path (CT-215).
- lane_rates: select the rate with the latest effective date when two rates are
  in effect at the same lane level, so newer Portland-Boise amendments apply
  (CT-214).
- road_use_tax: apply the 2% bulk filing discount as a reduction (0.98x) instead
  of a near-doubling multiplier (1.98x) once taxable miles exceed 1,000, so
  long-haul Oregon filings are no longer overstated (CT-208).
- eta_planner: count the remaining 14-hour window in exact minutes (60 per
  hour, not 59), so a replanned long-haul leg no longer runs past the window
  close instead of stopping for the 10-hour reset (CT-211).
- mode_conversion_factor: drop the stray +0.0001 uplift on the truckload-to-drayage
  base factor and on the drayage hazmat adjustment, so plain conversions use the
  configured 0.7600 base and hazmat drayage stacks to 0.7700 (CT-212, CT-209).
- Fix linehaul overweight permit premium from 0.11 to 0.10 per mile so
  multi-premium loads rate correctly (CT-202).
- Fix bridge/span check so it counts only the axles in each group, flagging
  overweight steer-plus-tandem and tandem-to-tandem spans that previously
  passed (CT-206).
- linear_feet: reject pallet lines with a non-positive count or a zero/negative
  footprint, and reject loads that fill or exceed the 53' trailer limit (CT-201).
- Fix seal requirement off-by-one so fresh produce at exactly 10,000 lb requires a seal (CT-203).

from decimal import Decimal

24.title: [CT-220] Restore leading zeros in numeric ZIP+4 imports
24.description:
Spreadsheet numerics that lost leading zeros from a ZIP+4 (for example 21341234 or 21341234.0) were split as a 5-digit ZIP plus a 3-digit extension and rejected. Bare values of 6-8 digits are now zero-padded back to 9 before splitting, so 21341234 becomes 02134-1234 and 8601234 becomes 00860-1234. Hyphen, 9-digit, Canadian and garbage handling are unchanged.

Tests: ran the full suite with pytest (287 passed). Added test_short_numeric_zip_plus_four_restores_leading_zeros, which failed before the fix.

"""Normalize US ZIP and Canadian postal codes from customer imports.

Customers send us stop lists as spreadsheets, and spreadsheets mangle postal codes:
a ZIP is stored as a number, so New England, New Jersey and Puerto Rico ZIPs lose
their leading zeros ("02134" becomes 2134, "00601" becomes 601), and sometimes come
back as floats ("2134.0"). Geocoding and lane rating both key on the normalized
form, so every address goes through ``normalize_postal_code`` on import.

Normalized forms:
    US:     "02134" or "02134-1234"
    Canada: "K1A 0B1"
"""

import re

_CANADIAN = re.compile(r"^([A-Z]\d[A-Z])\s?(\d[A-Z]\d)$")
_FLOAT_SUFFIX = re.compile(r"\.0+$")
# A ZIP that lost leading zeros: 3-4 digits for a 5-digit ZIP, 7-8 for ZIP+4.
_SHORT_ZIP5 = (3, 4)
_SHORT_ZIP9 = (6, 8)


def _clean_text(raw: str | int) -> str:
    text = str(raw).strip().upper()
    return _FLOAT_SUFFIX.sub("", text)


def _canadian(text: str) -> str | None:
    match = _CANADIAN.match(text)
    if not match:
        return None
    return f"{match.group(1)} {match.group(2)}"


def _us_parts(text: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
    """Split a US ZIP into its 5-digit ZIP and optional +4, restoring lost zeros."""
    if "-" in text:
        zip5, _, plus4 = text.partition("-")
        if len(zip5) in _SHORT_ZIP5:
            zip5 = zip5.zfill(5)
        return zip5, plus4
    digits = text.replace(" ", "")
    if len(digits) in _SHORT_ZIP5:
        return digits.zfill(5), None
    if len(digits) <= 5:
        return digits, None
    # Without a hyphen, the last four digits are the +4.
    if not (len(digits) in _SHORT_ZIP9):
        digits = digits.zfill(9)
    return digits[:5], digits[5:]


def _validate_us(zip5: str, plus4: str | None, raw: str | int) -> None:
    if len(zip5) != 5 or not zip5.isdigit():
        raise ValueError(f"not a US ZIP code: {raw!r}")
    if plus4 is not None and (len(plus4) != 4 or not plus4.isdigit()):
        raise ValueError(f"bad ZIP+4 extension: {raw!r}")


def normalize_postal_code(raw: str | int) -> str:
    """Return the normalized US ZIP or Canadian postal code, or raise ValueError.

    Accepts strings or ints. Leading zeros lost by a spreadsheet are restored, for
    both 5-digit ZIPs and ZIP+4.
    """
    text = _clean_text(raw)
    if not text:
        raise ValueError("empty postal code")
    canadian = _canadian(text)
    if canadian:
        return canadian
    zip5, plus4 = _us_parts(text)
    _validate_us(zip5, plus4, raw)
    return f"{zip5}-{plus4}" if plus4 else zip5

CHANGELOG.md:
# Changelog

All notable changes to carrier-utils.

## Unreleased

- drug_testing_pool_requirement: divide a quarterly target by the four quarters
  in a year instead of three, so period 3 no longer spreads the whole remaining
  obligation into a single period and the pool requirement is not overstated
  (CT-223).
- fuel_purchase_allocation: treat a zero-mile odometer span as valid and skip
  invalid trips instead of aborting, so an all-zero-mile eligible set allocates
  the purchase to the first eligible trip rather than dropping the fuel buy from
  settlement (CT-221).
- scorecard: add regression coverage for the on-time KPI so late deliveries
  excused by customer, consignee or weather codes stay out of the measured
  denominator, while on-time and unexcused late loads remain the only measured
  deliveries (CT-218).
- maintenance_fund_contribution: take the revenue-plan branch when a
  revenue_percent is configured instead of falling through to the flat path and
  withholding $0.00, so settlements with linehaul revenue at or above the $300
  threshold are assessed 2.5% of linehaul even with zero loaded miles (CT-219).
- bol_reference_parser: preserve all-zero numeric payloads instead of defaulting
  them to "1", so short PU/PICKUP references such as a one-character value or
  "000" are kept as entered rather than rewritten (CT-210).
- detention: start free time at the later of check-in and the appointment time
  (check-in only at FCFS stops) instead of at check-in whenever an appointment
  exists, so drivers who check in early are no longer billed detention for time
  inside the free-time window (CT-224).
- drug_testing_pool_requirement: spread the annual target across all 12 monthly
  periods instead of 11, so the period-12 compliance run returns a capped
  requirement rather than dividing by zero and crashing (CT-216).
- trailer_inspection_due: tighten the calendar limit after a failed inspection
  with `min` instead of `max`, so the 7-day reinspection rule overrides the
  normal 45/60/90-day interval instead of extending it (CT-217).
- team_driver_premium: apply the tiered team premium at exactly 300 miles
  instead of treating the boundary as short-haul, and apply contract
  multiplier before the flat add-on on the contracted path (CT-215).
- lane_rates: select the rate with the latest effective date when two rates are
  in effect at the same lane level, so newer Portland-Boise amendments apply
  (CT-214).
- road_use_tax: apply the 2% bulk filing discount as a reduction (0.98x) instead
  of a near-doubling multiplier (1.98x) once taxable miles exceed 1,000, so
  long-haul Oregon filings are no longer overstated (CT-208).
- eta_planner: count the remaining 14-hour window in exact minutes (60 per
  hour, not 59), so a replanned long-haul leg no longer runs past the window
  close instead of stopping for the 10-hour reset (CT-211).
- mode_conversion_factor: drop the stray +0.0001 uplift on the truckload-to-drayage
  base factor and on the drayage hazmat adjustment, so plain conversions use the
  configured 0.7600 base and hazmat drayage stacks to 0.7700 (CT-212, CT-209).
- Fix linehaul overweight permit premium from 0.11 to 0.10 per mile so
  multi-premium loads rate correctly (CT-202).
- Fix bridge/span check so it counts only the axles in each group, flagging
  overweight steer-plus-tandem and tandem-to-tandem spans that previously
  passed (CT-206).
- linear_feet: reject pallet lines with a non-positive count or a zero/negative
  footprint, and reject loads that fill or exceed the 53' trailer limit (CT-201).
- Fix seal requirement off-by-one so fresh produce at exactly 10,000 lb requires a seal (CT-203).
- Fix weekend tender expiry: Saturday is no longer treated as a business day, so
  Friday-evening and weekend tenders carry through to Monday 07:00 local and
  expire at 09:00 local (CT-204).
- reefer_monitor: end an excursion at the last reading received, marked not
  closed, when the logger goes quiet more than 15 minutes while out of range
  (CT-205).
- toll_allocation: ignore waived, $0.00 and zero-mile toll segments instead of
  rejecting the invoice run, so the remaining valid segments still allocate
  (CT-213).
- Fix EDI 997 overage comparison: the overage rate was always computed as zero,
  so acknowledgements exceeding the overage tolerance were reported as ACCEPTED
  instead of COUNT_MISMATCH (CT-207).

## 2026.10.29

- Carrier Tools library baseline for Q4.

2026-10-25 carrier-tools-bots: carrier-utils baseline
