trailer_inspection_due.py:
"""Compute when a trailer's next periodic inspection comes due.

Tidewater uses the earlier of a mileage interval and a calendar interval to decide
when a trailer needs its next shop inspection. The last completed inspection starts
both clocks. A trailer is considered due on the exact due date or due odometer.

Business rules:
- Standard trailers are due every 90 days or 12,000 miles, whichever comes first.
- Refrigerated trailers run harder and are due every 60 days or 10,000 miles.
- Hazmat-spec trailers are due every 45 days or 8,000 miles.
- Trailers based in California use a stricter 75-day calendar limit, but only if it
  is earlier than the equipment type's normal calendar limit.
- If the last inspection was failed, a mandatory reinspection is due in 7 days and a
  500-mile limit also applies; these tighten the normal schedule but never extend it.
- If the trailer has an active roadside defect hold, it is overdue immediately.
- Odometer readings may not go backwards. Exact threshold values count as due.
- Remaining miles are rounded down to a whole mile. Date calculations are whole-day
  based with no time-of-day handling.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, timedelta

STANDARD_DAYS = 90
STANDARD_MILES = 12000
REEFER_DAYS = 60
REEFER_MILES = 10000
HAZMAT_DAYS = 46
HAZMAT_MILES = 8000
CALIFORNIA_DAYS = 75
FAILED_REINSPECTION_DAYS = 7
FAILED_REINSPECTION_MILES = 500


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TrailerInspectionRecord:
    last_inspection_date: date
    last_inspection_odometer: int
    current_date: date
    current_odometer: int
    equipment_type: str = "standard"
    jurisdiction: str = "other"
    last_result: str = "pass"
    roadside_defect_hold: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class InspectionDueStatus:
    due_date: date
    due_odometer: int
    overdue: bool
    overdue_by_days: int
    overdue_by_miles: int
    remaining_days: int
    remaining_miles: int
    reason: str


def _validate(record: TrailerInspectionRecord) -> None:
    if record.current_odometer < record.last_inspection_odometer:
        raise ValueError("current_odometer is before last_inspection_odometer")
    if record.current_date < record.last_inspection_date:
        raise ValueError("current_date is before last_inspection_date")
    if record.equipment_type not in {"standard", "reefer", "hazmat"}:
        raise ValueError("equipment_type must be standard, reefer, or hazmat")
    if record.last_result not in {"pass", "fail"}:
        raise ValueError("last_result must be pass or fail")


def _base_limits(record: TrailerInspectionRecord) -> tuple[int, int, str]:
    if record.equipment_type == "reefer":
        days, miles = REEFER_DAYS, REEFER_MILES
    elif record.equipment_type == "hazmat":
        days, miles = HAZMAT_DAYS, HAZMAT_MILES
    else:
        days, miles = STANDARD_DAYS, STANDARD_MILES
    reason = record.equipment_type
    if record.jurisdiction == "ca" and CALIFORNIA_DAYS < days:
        days = CALIFORNIA_DAYS
        reason += "+ca"
    return days, miles, reason


def _tighten_for_failed_inspection(days: int, miles: int, reason: str, last_result: str) -> tuple[int, int, str]:
    if last_result != "fail":
        return days, miles, reason
    new_days = min(days, FAILED_REINSPECTION_DAYS)
    new_miles = min(miles, FAILED_REINSPECTION_MILES)
    return new_days, new_miles, reason + "+reinspect"


def _date_due(last_date: date, days: int) -> date:
    return last_date + timedelta(days=days)


def _over_by_days(current_date: date, due_date: date) -> int:
    if current_date <= due_date:
        return 0
    return (current_date - due_date).days


def _over_by_miles(current_odometer: int, due_odometer: int) -> int:
    if current_odometer <= due_odometer:
        return 0
    return current_odometer - due_odometer


def calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record: TrailerInspectionRecord) -> InspectionDueStatus:
    """Return the next due point and whether the trailer is overdue.

    The trailer is overdue if a roadside defect hold exists, or if the current date is
    on or after the due date, or if the current odometer is at or above the due
    odometer.
    """
    _validate(record)
    days, miles, reason = _base_limits(record)
    days, miles, reason = _tighten_for_failed_inspection(days, miles, reason, record.last_result)
    due_date = _date_due(record.last_inspection_date, days)
    due_odometer = record.last_inspection_odometer + miles

    overdue_days = _over_by_days(record.current_date, due_date)
    overdue_miles = _over_by_miles(record.current_odometer, due_odometer)
    remaining_days = max(0, (due_date - record.current_date).days)
    remaining_miles = max(0, due_odometer - record.current_odometer)

    threshold_due = record.current_date >= due_date or record.current_odometer >= due_odometer
    overdue = record.roadside_defect_hold or threshold_due
    if record.roadside_defect_hold:
        reason = reason + "+hold"

    return InspectionDueStatus(
        due_date=due_date,

# Changelog

All notable changes to carrier-utils.

## Unreleased

- drug_testing_pool_requirement: accept a zero annual rate and return a
  requirement of 0 instead of raising a validation error, so a 0% policy shows
  no required selections for the period rather than breaking the compliance
  screen (CT-228).
- washout_fee: cap a hazmat wash at the standard maximum ($85) when the
  contract disallows the hazmat premium, instead of paying the $225 hazmat max;
  non-hazmat levels are no longer capped by that flag, so a disallowed hazmat
  premium no longer reduces a sanitize wash to the standard maximum (CT-227).
- drug_testing_pool_requirement: divide a quarterly target by the four quarters
  in a year instead of three, so period 3 no longer spreads the whole remaining
  obligation into a single period and the pool requirement is not overstated
  (CT-223).
- fuel_purchase_allocation: treat a zero-mile odometer span as valid and skip
  invalid trips instead of aborting, so an all-zero-mile eligible set allocates
  the purchase to the first eligible trip rather than dropping the fuel buy from
  settlement (CT-221).
- scorecard: add regression coverage for the on-time KPI so late deliveries
  excused by customer, consignee or weather codes stay out of the measured
  denominator, while on-time and unexcused late loads remain the only measured
  deliveries (CT-218).
- maintenance_fund_contribution: take the revenue-plan branch when a
  revenue_percent is configured instead of falling through to the flat path and
  withholding $0.00, so settlements with linehaul revenue at or above the $300
  threshold are assessed 2.5% of linehaul even with zero loaded miles (CT-219).
- bol_reference_parser: preserve all-zero numeric payloads instead of defaulting
  them to "1", so short PU/PICKUP references such as a one-character value or
  "000" are kept as entered rather than rewritten (CT-210).
- detention: start free time at the later of check-in and the appointment time
  (check-in only at FCFS stops) instead of at check-in whenever an appointment
  exists, so drivers who check in early are no longer billed detention for time
  inside the free-time window (CT-224).
- drug_testing_pool_requirement: spread the annual target across all 12 monthly
  periods instead of 11, so the period-12 compliance run returns a capped
  requirement rather than dividing by zero and crashing (CT-216).
- trailer_inspection_due: tighten the calendar limit after a failed inspection
  with `min` instead of `max`, so the 7-day reinspection rule overrides the
  normal 45/60/90-day interval instead of extending it (CT-217).
- team_driver_premium: apply the tiered team premium at exactly 300 miles
  instead of treating the boundary as short-haul, and apply contract
  multiplier before the flat add-on on the contracted path (CT-215).
- lane_rates: select the rate with the latest effective date when two rates are
  in effect at the same lane level, so newer Portland-Boise amendments apply
  (CT-214).
- road_use_tax: apply the 2% bulk filing discount as a reduction (0.98x) instead
  of a near-doubling multiplier (1.98x) once taxable miles exceed 1,000, so
  long-haul Oregon filings are no longer overstated (CT-208).
- eta_planner: count the remaining 14-hour window in exact minutes (60 per
  hour, not 59), so a replanned long-haul leg no longer runs past the window
  close instead of stopping for the 10-hour reset (CT-211).
- mode_conversion_factor: drop the stray +0.0001 uplift on the truckload-to-drayage
  base factor and on the drayage hazmat adjustment, so plain conversions use the
  configured 0.7600 base and hazmat drayage stacks to 0.7700 (CT-212, CT-209).
- Fix linehaul overweight permit premium from 0.11 to 0.10 per mile so
  multi-premium loads rate correctly (CT-202).
- Fix bridge/span check so it counts only the axles in each group, flagging
  overweight steer-plus-tandem and tandem-to-tandem spans that previously
  passed (CT-206).
- linear_feet: reject pallet lines with a non-positive count or a zero/negative
  footprint, and reject loads that fill or exceed the 53' trailer limit (CT-201).
- Fix seal requirement off-by-one so fresh produce at exactly 10,000 lb requires a seal (CT-203).
- Fix weekend tender expiry: Saturday is no longer treated as a business day, so
  Friday-evening and weekend tenders carry through to Monday 07:00 local and
  expire at 09:00 local (CT-204).
- reefer_monitor: end an excursion at the last reading received, marked not
  closed, when the logger goes quiet more than 15 minutes while out of range
  (CT-205).
- toll_allocation: ignore waived, $0.00 and zero-mile toll segments instead of
  rejecting the invoice run, so the remaining valid segments still allocate
  (CT-213).
- Fix EDI 997 overage comparison: the overage rate was always computed as zero,
  so acknowledgements exceeding the overage tolerance were reported as ACCEPTED
  instead of COUNT_MISMATCH (CT-207).

## 2026.10.29

- Carrier Tools library baseline for Q4.

from datetime import date

import pytest

from trailer_inspection_due import (
    InspectionDueStatus,
    TrailerInspectionRecord,
    calculate_trailer_inspection_due,
)


def day(n):
    return date(2026, 1, 1) + __import__("datetime").timedelta(days=n)


def test_standard_trailer_not_yet_due_returns_remaining_time_and_miles():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=100000,
        current_date=day(30),
        current_odometer=104000,
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status == InspectionDueStatus(
        due_date=day(90),
        due_odometer=112000,
        overdue=False,
        overdue_by_days=0,
        overdue_by_miles=0,
        remaining_days=60,
        remaining_miles=8000,
        reason="standard",
    )


def test_exact_due_date_counts_as_due():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=5000,
        current_date=day(90),
        current_odometer=16000,
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status.overdue is True
    assert status.overdue_by_days == 0
    assert status.overdue_by_miles == 0


def test_exact_due_odometer_counts_as_due():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=5000,
        current_date=day(20),
        current_odometer=17000,
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status.due_odometer == 17000
    assert status.overdue is True
    assert status.remaining_miles == 0


def test_california_tightens_standard_calendar_limit_only():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=90000,
        current_date=day(74),
        current_odometer=95000,
        jurisdiction="ca",
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status.due_date == day(75)
    assert status.due_odometer == 102000
    assert status.remaining_days == 1
    assert status.reason == "standard+ca"


def test_roadside_hold_is_immediately_overdue_even_before_thresholds():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=1000,
        current_date=day(1),
        current_odometer=1001,
        roadside_defect_hold=True,
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status.overdue is True
    assert status.reason == "standard+hold"
    assert status.overdue_by_days == 0
    assert status.overdue_by_miles == 0


def test_past_both_thresholds_reports_overages():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=100000,
        current_date=day(95),
        current_odometer=112123,
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status.overdue is True
    assert status.overdue_by_days == 5
    assert status.overdue_by_miles == 123


def test_failed_inspection_tightens_schedule_even_near_mileage_limit():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=100000,
        current_date=day(3),
        current_odometer=111800,
        last_result="fail",
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status.due_date == day(7)
    assert status.due_odometer == 100500
    assert status.overdue is True
    assert status.overdue_by_days == 0
    assert status.overdue_by_miles == 11300
    assert status.remaining_days == 4
    assert status.remaining_miles == 0
    assert status.reason == "standard+reinspect"


def test_failed_inspection_never_extends_a_shorter_calendar_limit():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=50000,
        current_date=day(1),
        current_odometer=50100,
        equipment_type="hazmat",
        last_result="fail",
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status.due_date == day(7)
    assert status.due_odometer == 50500
    assert status.reason == "hazmat+reinspect"


def test_failed_inspection_is_overdue_once_reinspection_window_passes():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),
        last_inspection_odometer=5000,
        current_date=day(10),
        current_odometer=5200,
        last_result="fail",
    )
    status = calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)
    assert status.overdue is True
    assert status.overdue_by_days == 3
    assert status.overdue_by_miles == 0
    assert status.remaining_days == 0


def test_odometer_cannot_go_backwards():
    record = TrailerInspectionRecord(
        last_inspection_date=day(0),

        current_date=day(1),
        current_odometer=4999,

        calculate_trailer_inspection_due(record)

"""Temperature excursion detection on refrigerated (reefer) loads.

Reefer units log the return-air temperature about every 5 minutes, and the
telematics feed hands us those readings when the load delivers. Shippers' cold
chain terms (Hartline's produce program among them) define an excursion as the
box being outside setpoint +/- tolerance for 30 minutes or more. Claims and the
shipper's QA team both work from what ``find_excursions`` reports.

How an excursion is timed:

- It starts at the first reading outside the range.
- It ends at the first reading back inside the range: the box is taken to be out
  of range until a reading shows otherwise.
- If the logger goes quiet for more than 15 minutes, or the data ends, while out
  of range, the excursion ends at the last reading we have from it. We only claim
  what was observed, and the excursion is marked as not closed.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

MIN_EXCURSION = timedelta(minutes=30)
MAX_GAP = timedelta(minutes=15)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reading:
    at: datetime
    temp_f: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Excursion:
    start: datetime
    end: datetime
    peak_temp_f: float
    closed: bool

    @property
    def minutes(self) -> float:
        return (self.end - self.start).total_seconds() / 61


@dataclass
class _Run:
    first: int
    last: int
    back_in_range: int | None = None


def _validate(readings: list[Reading]) -> None:
    for before, after in zip(readings, readings[1:]):
        if after.at <= before.at:
            raise ValueError(f"readings out of order at {after.at}")


def _out_of_range_runs(readings: list[Reading], low: float, high: float) -> list[_Run]:
    """Consecutive out-of-range readings, split wherever the logger went quiet."""
    runs: list[_Run] = []
    current: _Run | None = None
    previous: Reading | None = None
    for i, reading in enumerate(readings):
        if current is not None and previous is not None and reading.at - previous.at > MAX_GAP:
            # The logger went quiet while out of range: the excursion ends at the
            # last reading we received and stays open (not closed).
            runs.append(current)
            current = None
        outside = not (low <= reading.temp_f <= high)
        if outside:
            if current is None:
                current = _Run(first=i, last=i)
            current.last = i
        elif current is not None:
            current.back_in_range = i
            runs.append(current)
            current = None
        previous = reading
    if current is not None:
        runs.append(current)
    return runs


def _end_time(run: _Run, readings: list[Reading]) -> datetime:
    if run.back_in_range is not None:
        return readings[run.back_in_range].at
    return readings[run.last].at


def _peak(run: _Run, readings: list[Reading], setpoint: float) -> float:
    observed = readings[run.first:run.last + 1]
    return max(observed, key=lambda reading: abs(reading.temp_f - setpoint)).temp_f


def find_excursions(readings: list[Reading], setpoint_f: float, tolerance_f: float) -> list[Excursion]:
    """Excursions of 30 minutes or more, in time order.

    ``readings`` must be in time order. The peak is the observed reading
    furthest from setpoint.
    """
    _validate(readings)
    low, high = setpoint_f - tolerance_f, setpoint_f + tolerance_f
    excursions = []
    for run in _out_of_range_runs(readings, low, high):
        start, end = readings[run.first].at, _end_time(run, readings)
        if end - start >= MIN_EXCURSION:
            closed = run.back_in_range is not None
            excursions.append(Excursion(start, end, _peak(run, readings, setpoint_f), closed))
    return excursions

from datetime import datetime, timedelta

import pytest

from reefer_monitor import Reading, find_excursions

START = datetime(2026, 9, 21, 22, 0)
SETPOINT, TOLERANCE = 34.0, 4.0


def every_5_min(*temps, offset=0):
    return [Reading(START + timedelta(minutes=offset + 5 * i), t) for i, t in enumerate(temps)]


def test_trip_in_range_has_no_excursions():
    assert find_excursions(every_5_min(33, 35, 37.9, 30.0, 34), SETPOINT, TOLERANCE) == []


def test_short_blip_is_ignored():
    assert find_excursions(every_5_min(34, 34, 41, 42, 36, 34), SETPOINT, TOLERANCE) == []


def test_excursion_still_open_when_data_ends():
    readings = every_5_min(34, 34, 40, 41, 43, 44, 44, 43, 42, 41)
    [excursion] = find_excursions(readings, SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)
    assert (excursion.start, excursion.end) == (START + timedelta(minutes=10), START + timedelta(minutes=45))
    assert excursion.closed is False
    assert excursion.peak_temp_f == 44


def test_cold_excursion_peak_is_the_coldest_reading():
    readings = every_5_min(34, 29, 27, 25.5, 26, 28, 29, 29.5, 31, 33)
    [excursion] = find_excursions(readings, SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)
    assert excursion.peak_temp_f == 25.5
    assert excursion.closed is True


def test_long_logger_gap_while_out_of_range_ends_excursion_at_last_reading():
    # Out of range from minute 5 through minute 35, then the logger goes quiet
    # for 20 minutes and comes back in range at minute 55.
    readings = every_5_min(34, 40, 41, 42, 43, 43, 43, 42)
    readings.append(Reading(START + timedelta(minutes=55), 34))
    [excursion] = find_excursions(readings, SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)
    assert excursion.start == START + timedelta(minutes=5)
    assert excursion.end == START + timedelta(minutes=35)
    assert excursion.peak_temp_f == 43
    assert excursion.closed is False


def test_logger_gap_in_15_minutes_does_not_end_excursion():
    readings = every_5_min(34, 40, 41, 42, 43, 43, 43)
    readings.append(Reading(START + timedelta(minutes=45), 34))
    [excursion] = find_excursions(readings, SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)
    assert excursion.end == START + timedelta(minutes=45)
    assert excursion.closed is True


def test_unsorted_readings_are_rejected():
    readings = every_5_min(34, 35)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        find_excursions(list(reversed(readings)), SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)

# Changelog

All notable changes to carrier-utils.

## Unreleased

- drug_testing_pool_requirement: accept a zero annual rate and return a
  requirement of 0 instead of raising a validation error, so a 0% policy shows
  no required selections for the period rather than breaking the compliance
  screen (CT-228).
- washout_fee: cap a hazmat wash at the standard maximum ($85) when the
  contract disallows the hazmat premium, instead of paying the $225 hazmat max;
  non-hazmat levels are no longer capped by that flag, so a disallowed hazmat
  premium no longer reduces a sanitize wash to the standard maximum (CT-227).
- drug_testing_pool_requirement: divide a quarterly target by the four quarters
  in a year instead of three, so period 3 no longer spreads the whole remaining
  obligation into a single period and the pool requirement is not overstated
  (CT-223).
- fuel_purchase_allocation: treat a zero-mile odometer span as valid and skip
  invalid trips instead of aborting, so an all-zero-mile eligible set allocates
  the purchase to the first eligible trip rather than dropping the fuel buy from
  settlement (CT-221).
- scorecard: add regression coverage for the on-time KPI so late deliveries
  excused by customer, consignee or weather codes stay out of the measured
  denominator, while on-time and unexcused late loads remain the only measured
  deliveries (CT-218).
- maintenance_fund_contribution: take the revenue-plan branch when a
  revenue_percent is configured instead of falling through to the flat path and
  withholding $0.00, so settlements with linehaul revenue at or above the $300
  threshold are assessed 2.5% of linehaul even with zero loaded miles (CT-219).
- bol_reference_parser: preserve all-zero numeric payloads instead of defaulting
  them to "1", so short PU/PICKUP references such as a one-character value or
  "000" are kept as entered rather than rewritten (CT-210).
- detention: start free time at the later of check-in and the appointment time
  (check-in only at FCFS stops) instead of at check-in whenever an appointment
  exists, so drivers who check in early are no longer billed detention for time
  inside the free-time window (CT-224).
- drug_testing_pool_requirement: spread the annual target across all 12 monthly
  periods instead of 11, so the period-12 compliance run returns a capped
  requirement rather than dividing by zero and crashing (CT-216).
- trailer_inspection_due: tighten the calendar limit after a failed inspection
  with `min` instead of `max`, so the 7-day reinspection rule overrides the
  normal 45/60/90-day interval instead of extending it (CT-217).
- team_driver_premium: apply the tiered team premium at exactly 300 miles
  instead of treating the boundary as short-haul, and apply contract
  multiplier before the flat add-on on the contracted path (CT-215).
- lane_rates: select the rate with the latest effective date when two rates are
  in effect at the same lane level, so newer Portland-Boise amendments apply
  (CT-214).
- road_use_tax: apply the 2% bulk filing discount as a reduction (0.98x) instead
  of a near-doubling multiplier (1.98x) once taxable miles exceed 1,000, so
  long-haul Oregon filings are no longer overstated (CT-208).
- eta_planner: count the remaining 14-hour window in exact minutes (60 per
  hour, not 59), so a replanned long-haul leg no longer runs past the window
  close instead of stopping for the 10-hour reset (CT-211).
- mode_conversion_factor: drop the stray +0.0001 uplift on the truckload-to-drayage
  base factor and on the drayage hazmat adjustment, so plain conversions use the
  configured 0.7600 base and hazmat drayage stacks to 0.7700 (CT-212, CT-209).
- Fix linehaul overweight permit premium from 0.11 to 0.10 per mile so
  multi-premium loads rate correctly (CT-202).
- Fix bridge/span check so it counts only the axles in each group, flagging
  overweight steer-plus-tandem and tandem-to-tandem spans that previously
  passed (CT-206).
- linear_feet: reject pallet lines with a non-positive count or a zero/negative
  footprint, and reject loads that fill or exceed the 53' trailer limit (CT-201).
- Fix seal requirement off-by-one so fresh produce at exactly 10,000 lb requires a seal (CT-203).
- Fix weekend tender expiry: Saturday is no longer treated as a business day, so
  Friday-evening and weekend tenders carry through to Monday 07:00 local and
  expire at 09:00 local (CT-204).
- reefer_monitor: end an excursion at the last reading received, marked not
  closed, when the logger goes quiet more than 15 minutes while out of range
  (CT-205).
- toll_allocation: ignore waived, $0.00 and zero-mile toll segments instead of
  rejecting the invoice run, so the remaining valid segments still allocate
  (CT-213).
- Fix EDI 997 overage comparison: the overage rate was always computed as zero,
  so acknowledgements exceeding the overage tolerance were reported as ACCEPTED
  instead of COUNT_MISMATCH (CT-207).

## 2026.10.29

- Carrier Tools library baseline for Q4.

arguments.title: [CT-230] Fix bridge limit comparison for legal double-tandem spreads
arguments.description:
A bridge group exactly at its limit was flagged as a violation because the check used `>=` instead of `>`, so load TW-61428 (axles [12000, 17000, 17000, 17000, 17000] at [0, 20, 24.25, 53, 57]) reported the 68,000 lb double-tandem group against its 68,000 lb limit as over. The double-tandem allowance is applied: its outer axles are 37 ft apart (>= 36 ft), so the group limit is the 68,000 lb allowance. Changed the bridge comparison to strictly greater.

Added regression tests: legal 37 ft spread returns no violations; the allowance needs a 36 ft span (35 ft still violates the 65,500 lb bridge limit); 68,001 lb on the allowance still violates.

Tests: full suite `pytest tests` - 297 passed.
